# Good morning everyone. - 2026-09-27 15:01

**Date** 27 Sep 2026, 15:01 · **Duration** 3 min · **Captions** 16

_Processed entirely on-device: CPU_

## Topics

- eigenvalue
- eigenvector
- determinant
- diagonalize

## Key points

- These two ideas sit at the center of linear algebra, so it is worth going slowly.
- Those vectors are the eigenvectors, and the factor they stretch by is the eigenvalue.
- To find them we solve the characteristic equation of the matrix. The determinant of a minus lambda times the identity must equal zero.
- The determinant is a single number that tells you whether the matrix squashes space flat.
- If it is zero, there is a non-trivial solution, and that is exactly what we want.
- Symmetric matrices always have real eigenvalues. That is a useful guarantee.

## Follow up

None mentioned.

_Generated without an LLM - install the model for better notes._

## Glossary

_Explanations in Mizo ṭawng (Mizo)._

- **eigenvalue** — A scalar showing how much a matrix stretches a special direction (its eigenvector).
- **eigenvector** — A direction that a matrix only stretches or shrinks, without rotating it.
- **determinant** — A single number from a square matrix; zero means the matrix squashes space flat.
- **diagonalize** — Rewriting a matrix in a basis where it becomes a simple diagonal scaling.

## Transcript

**[00:00]** Good morning everyone.
> Zân ṭha mi zawng zawng.

**[00:02]** Today we will start with eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
> Vawiin hian eigenvalues leh eigenvectors nen kan ṭan dawn a ni.

**[00:08]** These two ideas sit at the center of linear algebra, so it is worth going slowly.
> Heng ngaihdan pahnihte hi linear algebra-a hmun pawimawh ber a ni a, chuvangin a tulh luih a ngai a ni.

**[00:15]** A matrix is a linear transformation.
> Matrix chu linear transformation a ni.

**[00:19]** It stretches, rotates and shears space.
> A lo darh a, a lo hawi a, a hmun a lo tihtîr a.

**[00:24]** For most vectors, applying the matrix changes both direction and length.
> Vector tam zawk tan chuan matrix hman chuan kawng leh a sei a lo danglam a ni.

**[00:31]** But a few special vectors only change length.
> Mahse, vector bik engemaw zat chuan a seizawng chauh a thlak a ni.

**[00:35]** Their direction is preserved.
> An kaihhruaina chu a awm reng reng a ni.

**[00:39]** Those vectors are the eigenvectors, and the factor they stretch by is the eigenvalue.
> Chu vector chu eigenvectors a ni a, a chhunga an inrawlhna factor chu eigenvalue a ni.

**[00:47]** To find them we solve the characteristic equation of the matrix. The determinant of a minus lambda times the identity must equal zero.
> An hmuh tur chuan matrix a characteristic equation kan lo chhut a, a nihna ang chuan zero a nih ngei tur a ni.

**[00:59]** The determinant is a single number that tells you whether the matrix squashes space flat.
> determinant hi matrix-in space flat a tihchhiat leh tihchilh loh chu a hrilhfiah theih nan number pakhat a ni.

**[01:07]** If it is zero, there is a non-trivial solution, and that is exactly what we want.
> Zero a nih chuan, thil dangdanglam lo awm a ni a, chu chu chu kan duh chiah chu a ni.

**[01:15]** Symmetric matrices always have real eigenvalues. That is a useful guarantee.
> Symmetric matrix-te chuan eigenvalues dik an nei reng a. Chu chu a tha taka a inpeihpui thei a ni.

**[01:23]** Once we have a full set of eigenvectors, we can diagonalize the matrix.
> eigenvectors set khat kan neih chuan matrix chu diagonalize kan ti thei ang.

**[01:30]** Diagonalization turns a hard repeated multiplication into a simple one.
> Diagonalization chuan a har leh repeated multiplication chu a simple a ni.

**[01:37]** We will use this next week when we look at principal component analysis.
> Hei hi a lo kalpui tur chu kan hmanpui dawn a ni.
